author: zeenobit
body:
# Objective

The current implementation of `RelationshipSourceCollection` only operates on `Entity`, some other specific entity containers. This prevents the relations to work on entity wrapper types, such as [`Instance<T>`](https://docs.rs/moonshine-kind/latest/moonshine_kind/struct.Instance.html). This PR aims to solve this.

## Solution

This changelist adds a new `RelationshipSourceItem` trait which is automatically implemented for `Entity`.

It also adds a new type entry to `RelationshipSourceCollection`:
```rust
pub trait RelationshipSourceCollection {
    /// The type of the [`Entity`]-like item stored in the collection.
    type Item: RelationshipSourceItem;
    ...
}
```

The rest of the CL is fairly straightforward as it's just conversion between "item" and entities. This allows `RelationshipSourceItem` to operate on any generic entity wrapper container.

## Testing

A simple test has been added to ensure correct behavior:
`generic_relationship_source_collections`

## Known Issues

There is currently no macro support for this; which means any component which uses non-Entity types for relations has to implement it manually. Let me know if that's a requirement for this PR to pass or if we'd like that in a separate PR.

author: aguilar1x
body:
Creation of the Tokenized Educational Content contract, its tests, and documentation.

Things accomplished in the contract:

- Content Management: Users can publish educational content by providing a title, content hash (pointing to off-chain storage), and subject tags. Each piece of content receives a unique ID and timestamps are automatically recorded.

- Upvoting System: Implements a secure upvoting mechanism with duplicate vote prevention, allowing community members to signal quality content while maintaining vote integrity.

- Verification Framework: Enables content verification to establish trust, with verified status displayed alongside upvotes. Content creators can also self-verify their submissions.

- Modular Architecture: The codebase is structured into specialized modules (publish, vote, verify, storage) for better maintainability and clear separation of concerns.

- Comprehensive Testing: Includes 15 detailed tests covering all aspects of functionality, edge cases, and complex interaction scenarios to ensure reliability.

- Event Emission: The contract emits events for significant actions (publishing, upvoting, verification) to facilitate off-chain tracking and indexing.

- [x] Closes #65

author: renegade334
body:
A few small cleanup bits for globals.d.ts.

- Improve the definitions for `gc()`, and avoid global scope pollution.
- Corrected a couple of `CallSite` definitions.
  - These V8 internals are not documented, but can be viewed at https://github.com/nodejs/node/blob/main/deps/v8/src/builtins/builtins-callsite.cc.
  - `getEnclosingColumnNumber()`, `getEnclosingLineNumber()` and `getScriptNameOrSourceURL()` can all return `null`.
  - `getFileName()` can return `null`, not `undefined`.
- Removed some docblocks from the DOM interfaces; these have a tendency to clash when lib.dom is loaded, and aren't documented in the Node API.
- Consolidated the DOM interfaces together for ease of maintenance.
- Moved globals tests from node-tests to test/globals, and removed remaining legacy content from node-tests

author: zixu-w
body:
When Swift visits an `ExtensionDecl` from an `@objc @implementation` extension, it fetches the implemented Objective-C interface declaration from the header file and adds to the visitor.
We don't want these API records from `APIGenRecorder` for Swift API descriptor, because we cannot correctly reason about their API access as they depend on the header group which Swift doesn't know about.

Resolves rdar://148943382

author: cshimm
body:
## Summary & Changes 📃 - Resolves #140 - **Summary:** These changes add the ability to fetch data from the shift table in Supabase, and display it on the front end. ## **Changes:** - Removed references to fields from old dummy data schema. - Displayed all data retrieved from Supabase on Shift Details component. - Introduced a dummy integer value `currentUserId`. This will likely be set on login in a future iteration, but for now the definition exists in the shift details page itself. - Conditionally render "Give up shift" and "Take shift" buttons if the assigned user is equal to the `currentUserId`. Even though users won't be able to see other user's shifts, I added this as a safeguard, in case a shift from another user is loaded in their instance. - Introduced an RPC call to the `is_supervisor` function in Supabase, providing the current user Id to determine whether the user is a supervisor or not. - Conditionally render "Approve" and "Deny" buttons if user is a supervisor AND the assigned user id is **_not_** the current user Id. The idea behind this was to ensure that only a different supervisor can approve & deny shifts. This can be changed if needed. - Moved `setAMorPM` and to`12Hours` functions into new file `dateUtils.ts`. - Introduced `ShiftDetail` type - Introduced `supabaseAdminClient` to ensure necessary permissions when making call to RPC. - Moved the ExpoSecureStoreAdapter into new file `expoSecureStoreAdapter.ts`, exported and used in both `supabaseClient.ts` and `supabaseAdminClient.ts`. - The `needs_coverage` param on the Shift type was set to 'false' when it should have been set to 'boolean'. ## Screenshots / Visual Aids 🔎 📌 **Required for:** UI changes, layout updates, or bug fixes.
Expand ⬇️ Signed in as supervisor: ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47490dce-6c13-43b1-a1ed-ea1621643056) Signed in as regular user: ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bae96405-7089-46e8-aad9-9ac7ea9d9ae9)
## How to Test 🧪 - **Steps to Reproduce:** 1. Ensure your Supabase instance is running. 2. Run `npx expo install` if necessary. 3. Run `expo start` and run the device on your preferred device (web browser excluded) 4. On app launch, navigate to the main app (first link) 5. Back in the IDE, in the shift details file, note the `currentUserId` is set to `2`, which is a supervisor. 6. In the app, on the calendar page, navigate to the shift details page by tapping any of the grey agenda items. 7. The buttons say "APPROVE" and "DENY". 8. Back in the IDE, change the value of the `currentUserId` to `3`. 9. Refresh the app, navigate back to the calendar page then click the agenda item "Afternoon shift A". The `assignedUserId` for this shift is `3` so you should observe 2 buttons "GIVE UP SHIFT" and "TAKE SHIFT". 10. Go back to the calendar page and tap the agenda item underneath "Afternoon shift B". the `assignedUserId` for this shift is 4 and user id 3 is not a supervisor, so no buttons are rendered. For reference: Currently Ids 1 and 2 are supervisors. ## Checklist ✅ - [x] I have **tested** this PR **locally** and it works as expected. - [x] This PR **resolves an issue** (`Resolves #issue-number`). - [x] **Reviewers, assignees(self), tags, and labels** are correctly assigned. - [x] **Squash commits** and enable **auto-merge** if approved.

body:
## What changed / motivation ?

TypeScript types were invalid, fixed `StyleXTypes.d.ts` (`VarGroup` and `CSSType`) and added a compiled `VarTypes.d.ts` with conditions added to `CSSType` so type constraints are preserved.

For example:
```ts
(T extends (any extends Angle<infer R> ? R : never) ? Angle<T> : never)
```

Which resolves to:
```ts
(T extends string | 0 ? Angle<T> : never)
```

Instead of:
```ts
Angle<T>
```

Fixes #969

Note: PRs with titles not following the format will not be merged

## Problem Statement
<!--
Describe
- What problem are you trying to solve
- What issues or limitations exist in the current code
- Why this change is necessary 
-->
We store the successful execution IDs for each store in ZK path /<venice-cluster>/executionIds/succeededPerStore. This is like a checkpoint till what point we have successfully processed the admin messages for each store.
But when we delete a store, we do not clean this map. This can result into the size of this ZNode grow beyond the allowed limit of 1MB.
At this point, no admin messages can be updated into this, hence cannot be consumed, for ANY store in that cluster.

## Solution
<!--
Describe
- What changes you are making and why. 
- How these changes solve the problem.
- Any performance considerations or trade-offs. 
- Describe what testings you have done, for example, performance testing etc.
-->
This admin tool command will remove the entries for the deleted stores and help to reduce the size of this ZNode.
However, still it can reach to the max size and hence puts a limit to how many stores we can have in a venice cluster. Also note that there is a limit to how many children a ZNode can have (100K) which also limits the number of venice stores in a cluster.

This pull request introduces several improvements to the process of loading and visualizing biodiversity points on the interactive map. The changes primarily focus on optimizing data loading from the API and improving point visualization using the `leaflet.markercluster` library.

## Changes Made:

### Pagination of Points:
- A pagination mechanism was implemented to load all biodiversity points from the API.
- The system is now capable of iterating through all API pages, retrieving the full data set from the database without the need to limit the number of records in the initial request.

### Improved Point Clustering:
- The use of `leaflet.markercluster` was integrated to group biodiversity points into clusters, improving the user experience when viewing large amounts of data on the map.
- Each loaded point is dynamically added to a cluster group for easier visualization.

### Docker File Modification:
- The Docker configuration files were updated to facilitate the development environment, ensuring that application containers are correctly set up to support the new structure and changes in data loading.

## Current Limitations:

- **Performance**: As the data grows, map performance may be affected, especially on devices with lower capacity. Although clustering improves visualization, further optimization of data loading or the implementation of additional pagination or lazy loading techniques may be needed in the future.
  
- **Layer Synchronization**: Currently, the "Ibagué communes" layer is loaded independently and its visibility is separate from that of the biodiversity points. This could cause visual discrepancies if both layers are not handled properly.

## Next Steps:

- Implement a more advanced filtering system for the points, allowing users to select which types of records they wish to view based on various criteria.
  
- Optimize performance with large data volumes (possibly implementing techniques like smarter pagination or on-demand loading).
  
- Improve synchronization between different layers to ensure a smoother user experience.

## Description

This refactor eliminates duplicate RSS items for **reposted** Hacker News stories.  
Previously the RSS `<guid>` was the article URL, so reposts generated new GUIDs.  
Now we use the HN thread URL (`comment_link`) as the `<guid>`; every repost of the
same thread therefore re-uses the same GUID.

- Fixes [#421](https://github.com/k-zehnder/gophersignal/issues/421) – duplicate entries for reposts.

### Changes Made
- In `build_item`, set `<guid>` to `article.comment_link` and mark it `permalink=true`.
- If `comment_link` is absent, fall back to the **SHA-1 of the lower-cased title**.

### Testing
- Manually verified that reposted HN stories no longer create duplicate RSS items.

body:
## Overview
This PR implements a set of Clarity smart contracts for managing telecommunications services on the blockchain. The system enables telecom carriers to verify each other, share infrastructure, establish service level agreements, track usage, and settle payments automatically.

## Contracts Included

### 1. Provider Verification Contract
- Validates legitimate carriers in the telecommunications network
- Maintains a registry of verified providers
- Allows admin to add/remove providers from the verified list

### 2. Infrastructure Sharing Contract
- Manages joint use of network assets between carriers
- Allows providers to register their infrastructure assets
- Enables creation and management of sharing agreements
- Tracks availability and pricing of shared assets

### 3. Service Level Contract
- Records performance guarantees between carriers
- Defines uptime, latency, and bandwidth requirements
- Allows submission and disputing of performance reports
- Calculates penalties for SLA violations

### 4. Usage Tracking Contract
- Monitors service consumption across networks
- Records usage with details on quantity and pricing
- Provides verification mechanism for usage records
- Calculates costs based on recorded usage

### 5. Settlement Contract
- Handles automated inter-carrier payments
- Creates and processes settlement records
- Supports dispute resolution for payments
- Links settlements to usage records

## Implementation Notes
- All contracts use simple data structures to maintain clarity and efficiency
- Admin controls are implemented for sensitive operations
- Each contract includes appropriate error handling
- Read-only functions are provided for data retrieval
- Contracts are designed to work together as a cohesive system

## Testing
Tests are implemented using Vitest to verify the functionality of each contract.

## Future Improvements
- Integration with token contracts for actual value transfer
- Enhanced indexing for efficient data retrieval
- More sophisticated dispute resolution mechanisms
- Integration with off-chain oracles for performance monitoring

author: woct0rdho
body:
This is an alternative of #6589, and related to #4809 #6000

We add the Python ABI tag to the filename of each cached C binary, to avoid linking errors when the user switches the Python version.

According to the [comment](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/pull/4809#issuecomment-2376984522), I move the function `platform_key` to `triton.backends.driver`. The AMD-specific behavior can be implemented on top of this PR if needed.

I think `sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')` is the proper way to get the ABI tag. It supports Python 3.9 to 3.13, both Linux and Windows, and many kinds of Python distributions including the embedded and the standalone builds. It also distinguishes cp313 and cp313t ([free-threaded](https://docs.python.org/3/howto/free-threading-python.html)), which we may need in future. It has been used a few times in the codebase.

If I understand correctly, `sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')` also covers everything in `machine(), system(), *architecture()`, but for now I leave them as they are.

Note that this PR only focus on the C binaries. As of the current main branch, the cache hashes of CUDA binaries also depend on the Python version, but I think they should not, and we can discuss that later.

**Store Column Indexes in Dedicated Column (`s_col_indexes`)**

This change introduces a new special column named `s_col_indexes`, which stores the indexes of the data columns associated with each series.

This column will enable future optimizations by allowing readers to materialize only the necessary columns when accessing a series, reducing I/O and memory usage during queries.

body:
This pull request introduces several new features, enhancements, and fixes across multiple parts of the game, focusing on faction interactions, enemy behavior, and system integrations. Key changes include the addition of a Faction Battle System, enhancements to enemy group spawning and chaos mechanics, replacement of the "panic" state with a "rage" state for enemies, and updates to particle system usage.

### New Features and Systems:
- **Faction Battle System**: A new system enabling dynamic battles between enemy factions based on proximity and chaos levels. Includes features like detection, battle resolution, and integration with the Chaos and GroupManager systems.
- **Randomized Enemy Group Spawning**: Introduced a weighted spawning system that dynamically adjusts faction spawn rates based on player actions and game state, with features like faction surges and advanced chaos integration.

### Enhancements to Existing Systems:
- **Group Management**: Added new methods to the `GroupManager` for tracking and organizing entities by faction, including utilities for finding hostile enemies and managing group counts.
- **Chaos System Adjustment**: Increased the chaos adjustment value in the debug panel from 50 to 100 for more dramatic gameplay effects.

### Enemy Behavior Changes:
- **Rage State Implementation**: Replaced the "panic" state with a "rage" state for enemies, including new methods (`checkRageState`, `enterRageState`, `exitRageState`, etc.) and event emissions for rage-related behaviors. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-39839ed94b86a83668dc32a1d00ac1fb9547f5ea85c374975c9e6f8d6ba5336aL3-R3) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-39839ed94b86a83668dc32a1d00ac1fb9547f5ea85c374975c9e6f8d6ba5336aL270-R276) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-39839ed94b86a83668dc32a1d00ac1fb9547f5ea85c374975c9e6f8d6ba5336aL289-R290) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-39839ed94b86a83668dc32a1d00ac1fb9547f5ea85c374975c9e6f8d6ba5336aL309-R335) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-39839ed94b86a83668dc32a1d00ac1fb9547f5ea85c374975c9e6f8d6ba5336aL346-R355) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-39839ed94b86a83668dc32a1d00ac1fb9547f5ea85c374975c9e6f8d6ba5336aL367-R371) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-39839ed94b86a83668dc32a1d00ac1fb9547f5ea85c374975c9e6f8d6ba5336aR446-R455) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-39839ed94b86a83668dc32a1d00ac1fb9547f5ea85c374975c9e6f8d6ba5336aL467-R471)

### Fixes and Refactoring:
- **Particle System Update**: Refactored particle emitter creation to align with the updated Phaser API, fixing compatibility issues across multiple managers (`ChaosManager.js`, `UIManager.js`, `FactionBattleManager.js`, etc.).

These updates collectively enhance the game's strategic depth, visual feedback, and system integrations, while addressing technical debt and introducing new gameplay dynamics.

author: molereddy
body:
# What does this PR do?

Resolves several bugs related to narrow tokenization cases. 2, 3, 4 are interlinked issues and 1 is close to them as well. 

1. Log-probs
- Previously the `tokenwise_logprobs` and `tokenwise_vocab_logprobs` functions were inadvertently keeping the `eos` token in the label sequence, leading to the model being forced to predict `eos` token in the MIA (minK, minK++, gradnorm) and ES/EM metrics.
- This wasn't much of an issue w TOFU as the chat model predicts `eos` anyways, but still the original intention was to never get `eos` involved in these calculations.
- This became especially an issue with MUSE (which is not a chat model thus doesn't predict `eos`) leading to low ES scores issues (#100)
- This PR fixes the code, the results and existing evals are to be updated accordingly

2. Small target sequences getting mixed up w prompt
- For some models like Phi-1.5 which have weird tokenizers and for data points which have 1 word target labels, you may end up with the target words being tokenized into the prompt
- This PR warns about such cases and modifies ES and EM to set value as `None` in such cases

3. Handing empty label sequence cases
- When the above issue occurred, previously the code did not update both the labels and logprobs list, leading to mismatch and mixup across the batch which then led to failed asserts with Phi-1.5 [pointed out in #100] 
- This PR ensures empty tensors are sent in such cases

4. Date in system prompt
- Llama3.2 or 3.1 tokenizer inexplicably adds the current date to the chat template prompt, making results (slightly) irreproducible (#88)
- This PR allows for fixing the date for Llama through the model template args

5. Handling invalid values
- When a metric is evaluated to be `None` on a data point (usually due to tokenization issues), we set the aggregation to filter out such points and only compute on those that have values

6. Misc modifications
- The `tokenwise_logprobs` and `tokenwise_vocab_logprobs` involved changing model train mode. This was better handled in the evaluation metric code itself (used only by `gradnorm` MIA attack).
- Documentation fix to remove non-existent cfg file

Fixes # (issue)
#98
#100

author: poolgray34
body:
This Pull Request implements beam search decoding in the ChatGLM C++ backend. It addresses Issue #<issue_number> by providing a more sophisticated decoding algorithm than simple greedy decoding, potentially leading to higher quality generated text.

**Key changes:**

*   **`src/beam_search.h`:** Introduces the `beam_search` function and supporting data structures (e.g., `BeamSearchNode`) for performing beam search.
*   **`src/chatglm.cpp`:**
    *   Implements the `beam_search` algorithm using a priority queue to maintain the top `beam_size` candidate sequences.
    *   Adds `beam_search_generate` function, callable from Python, that sets up the beam search with the model state and necessary parameters.
    *   Refactors `generate` function for standard generation.
    *   Introduces `create_model_state` for managing model state.
    *   Introduces `model_forward` as api for main model forward step.
    *   Adds supporting functions to handle logits sampling, model state creation and forward pass calculations.
*   **`python/chatglm.cpp`:** Exposes the `beam_search_generate`,`create_model_state` and `model_forward` function to the Python interface using pybind11.
    * Exposes the chatglm config class
*   **`python/chatglm.py`:** Modifies the Python `ChatGLM` class to utilize the new `beam_search_generate` function and integrate the new api.

**Reasoning for changes:**

*   Beam search explores multiple possible sequences simultaneously, allowing the model to recover from suboptimal initial choices. This is achieved by maintaining a 'beam' of the `beam_size` most probable sequences at each step.
*   The C++ implementation provides performance benefits compared to a pure Python implementation, especially for computationally intensive operations like model inference.
*   The python api is modified to match the cpp implementation and make use of model state api.

**Testing:**

*   Added unit tests (not in this diff, pending implementation) to verify the correctness of the `beam_search` function.
*   Manually tested the `beam_search_generate` function in a Python environment, comparing the generated text with greedy decoding. Verified that beam search produces more coherent and contextually relevant outputs in several test cases.
*   The performance of the current beam search has been validated and deemed acceptable, but it is still subject to further optimization.

**Future improvements:**

*   Implement length normalization to prevent the algorithm from favoring shorter sequences.
*   Add more comprehensive test coverage, including edge cases and different model configurations.
*   Explore more efficient data structures and algorithms for maintaining the beam.
*   Add functionality for specifying a custom scoring function for candidate sequences.

author: sherif-mooo
body:
This PR refactors the OS‐abstraction “ProcessInteraction” layer to eliminate runtime polymorphism and vtable overhead by adopting the Curiously Recurring Template Pattern (CRTP). Key changes:

CRTP Interface

process_interaction.h now defines template<Derived> class ProcessInteraction with a single inline trampoline to Derived::GetProcessNameImpl().

The free-function GetProcessName() is declared inline in the header for clients, with its definition in the .cpp marked non-inline to allow LTO to inline across TUs.

Platform Implementations

Linux and QNX implementations (ProcessLinuxImpl and ProcessQnxImpl) now inherit from ProcessInteraction<Process*Impl> and implement GetProcessNameImpl().

Removed the old factory functions and virtual overrides.

author: adwinross
body:
# Description

Automatically track ViewController TTID as span.

## How it works

**ViewController load time** tracking works by monitoring the ViewController's lifecycle events:

1. The span starts in either the `loadView` or `viewDidLoad` callback of the ViewController:
   - If you inherit from `MsrViewController` (Swift) or `MSRViewController` (Objective-C), the span will start from `loadView`.
   - Otherwise, the span will start from `viewDidLoad`.
2. The span ends when `viewDidAppear` is called, indicating that the view is fully visible on screen.

Checkpoints that will be added to TTID spans:
- `vc_load_view` (only If you inherit from `MsrViewController` or `MSRViewController`)
- `vc_view_did_load`
- `vc_view_will_appear`
- `vc_view_did_appear`

## Related issue
Closes #2082

body:
### Changes

- Remove `item: Item` from `struct cursor_t` (aka `Cursor`) -- in fear of misuse by reentrant functions.
- Make `info` in `IpiCg` no longer a pointer to `IpiCgInfo`, but a copy -- as the item (`info` was extracted from) wasn't being held onto for long enough.
- Modify `ipiGraphCreateFromFile` to behave like `ipiGraphCreateFromMemory` -- moving reader position before when reading the graph.

- Install any extension with an update site. I tested it with the free DPCalendar upcoming module.

- Install the extension again.

There are two update sites for the same extension.

Only one update site for the extension.

author: obarroncs
body:
Arm Thumb2 has the concept of `IT Blocks`, which are a sequence of up to 4 instructions which each run conditionally based on a single initial condition defined in an IT instruction. This was a feature introduced to Thumb mode to allow for more efficient execution of conditional instructions, because Thumb mode instructions generally cannot be made conditional (while normal Arm instructions can).

There's a good overview of these instructions here - https://azeria-labs.com/arm-conditional-execution-and-branching-part-6/#:~:text=CONDITIONAL%20EXECUTION%20IN%20THUMB

Official docs: https://developer.arm.com/documentation/dui0473/m/arm-and-thumb-instructions/it


Once the Unicorn engine starts executing an IT block, it doesn't stop until all the instructions are executed, akin to it's behavior in MIPS branch delay slots. https://github.com/unicorn-engine/unicorn/issues/1630#:~:text=In%20short%2C%20it%20is%20similar%20to%20ARM%20that%20the%20condition%20might%20be%20lost%20if%20we%20stop%20inside%20a%20delay%20slot. The solution here is to disable the emulator in these blocks, since it skips over the instructions in the block that we still want to display.

body:
How maintenance in the the contrib repo works is kind of hidden away, and many people assume it works similarly to the core repo where there's shared ownership across the whole repo, which is not completely the case here.

This puts info about component ownership more prominently into the README.md, and clarifies that packages here are community maintained for the most part.

I plan to follow-up with a new document with role descriptions (split from CONTRIBUTING.md) to clarify further, as well as a new document for component maintenance status lifecycle (including a process for removal of unmaintained components).

body: Closes [#221234](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/221234) **Merging into a feature branch** ## Summary This PR adds: - The analytics index creation when the cases plugin starts. - Backfill task registration. - Backfill task scheduling. - Mapping version 1 for: - `.internal.cases` - `.internal.cases-comments` - `.internal.cases-attachments` - All corresponding painless scripts. ## How to review 1. The main functionality is in `analytics_index.ts`. The class in this file implements the index creation algorithm of the RFC. 2. Three folders instantiate this class to create the indexes we need: - `cases_analytics/cases_index/` - `cases_analytics/comments_index/` - `cases_analytics/attachments_index/` 3. The backfill logic can be found in `cases_analytics/tasks/backfill_task`. 4. I moved the `retry_service` previously used by the cases connector to a `common` folder and started using it in the `AnalyticsIndex` class. 5. The call to create the indexes is done in `x-pack/platform/plugins/shared/cases/server/plugin.ts`. ## How to test A few things are needed. 1. Create a role that has index creation permission. Below is what works for me; it might be overkill. 2. Create a user with the role created in step 1. Let's call the user `index_creator`. **The password should be** `changeme`. 6. Start Kibana with this user as the Elasticsearch user - `yarn start` with the option `--elasticsearch.username=index_creator`. 7. Kibana startup logs should show relevant messages: ``` [INFO ][plugins.cases] [.internal.cases] Checking if index exists. [INFO ][plugins.cases] [.internal.cases-attachments] Checking if index exists. [INFO ][plugins.cases] [.internal.cases-comments] Checking if index exists. ``` 8. You can check the content of these indexes in the Dev Tools. ``` GET /.internal.cases/_search GET /.internal.cases-comments/_search GET /.internal.cases-attachments/_search ``` 9. You can check the mapping of each of these indexes in the Dev Tools. ``` GET /.internal.cases GET /.internal.cases-comments GET /.internal.cases-attachments ``` 10. You can check the painless scripts in the Dev Tools. ``` GET /_scripts/cai_cases_script_1 GET /_scripts/cai_attachments_script_1 GET /_scripts/cai_comments_script_1 ```

author: frelon
body:
Commit 151b1994caad ("scxtop: better naming for kernel worker threads") introduces some code that does not compile for aarch64/riscv64:

```
error[E0308]: mismatched types
   --> tools/scxtop/src/lib.rs:473:57
    |
473 |                 let next_comm = unsafe { CStr::from_ptr(sched_switch.next_comm.as_ptr()) }
    |                                          -------------- ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ expected `*const u8`, found `*const i8`
    |                                          |
    |                                          arguments to this function are incorrect
    |
    = note: expected raw pointer `*const u8`
               found raw pointer `*const i8`
```

It seems the bindgen is outputting [i8; 16] for next_comm which means as_ptr returns a *const i8. Casting this to the platform dependant c_char (which translates to u8/i8 based on the platform) makes the code build on all platforms.

Fixes: 151b1994caad ("scxtop: better naming for kernel worker threads")

## 🚀 내가 새로 알게 된 점 **<체크박스 기능>** - 전체 선택 체크박스를 클릭하면 모든 개별 체크박스의 상태도 체크되는 기능을 구현하는데 시간이 꽤 걸렸습니다! - updateSelectAllState() 함수를 통해 개별 체크박스가 변경될 때, 전체 선택 체크박스의 상태를 업데이트하는 역할을 하도록 하였고, - selectAllCheckbox.addEventListener("change", ...) 이벤트 리스너를 통해서 전체 선택 체크박스를 클릭했을 때, 개별 체크박스들을 일괄적으로 체크/체크 해제할 수 있도록 기능을 구현했습니다. **<드래그앤드롭 기능>** - 할 일 항목을 드래그하여 순서를 변경할 수 있도록 HTML5의 Drag and Drop API를 사용하였고, 각 행에 draggable 속성을 설정하여 드래그 가능하도록 했습니다. - 드래그로 항목을 이동한 후, UI가 변경된 배열을 반영할 수 있도록 renderTodos()를 호출하여 화면을 새로 고침했습니다. - 상태를 로컬 저장소에 반영하는 saveTodos() 함수를 추가하여 데이터가 지속되도록 했습니다. **새로 알게 된 개념 💡 💡** - draggable 속성 및 이벤트 핸들링 각 행에 draggable="true" 속성을 추가하고, dragstart, dragover, drop 이벤트를 사용하여 드래그 앤 드롭을 처리했습니다. dragstart 이벤트에서는 드래그 중인 항목의 ID를 저장하고, dragover에서 e.preventDefault()를 호출하여 드롭이 가능하도록 설정했습니다. drop 이벤트에서는 드래그된 항목의 ID와 목표 위치의 항목 ID를 비교하여 배열에서 항목의 순서를 변경할 수 있었습니다. - 배열 순서 변경 및 UI 업데이트 todos 배열에서 항목의 순서를 변경하기 위해 splice 메서드를 사용하여 원래 항목을 제거하고 새 위치에 삽입했습니다. 변경된 배열은 saveTodos()와 renderTodos() 함수를 통해 저장하고 UI를 업데이트했습니다. - dataset을 사용한 데이터 관리 각 항목에 data-id 속성을 사용하여 고유 ID를 저장하고, dataset.id를 통해 드래그된 항목과 목표 항목을 식별했습니다. **시행착오 💭💭** - 드롭이 안 되는 이유는 dragover 때문! 처음에는 드래그는 되는데, 드롭이 동작하지 않았습니다. 알고 보니 HTML의 기본 동작에서는 drop이 허용되지 않기 때문에 dragover 이벤트에서 꼭 e.preventDefault()를 호출해줘야 하더라고요! 이걸 안 하면 drop 이벤트가 발생하지 않습니다. . - Drag & Drop API는 HTML5 내장 처음에는 따로 라이브러리를 써야 하나 싶었는데, HTML5에서 이미 제공하는 기본 API였습니다!
## 🤔 구현 과정에서의 어려웠던/고민했던 부분 Todo 리스트에 다양한 기능들이 포함되다 보니, CSS와 JavaScript 코드가 꽤 길어져 가독성이 떨어진다는 고민을 계속하게 되었습니다. 그래서 중복되는 스타일 속성은 최대한 묶어주고, JavaScript 함수도 간소화하며 중복되는 기능들은 공통 함수로 묶어주면서 작업을 진행했습니다. 하지만 여전히 최선의 코드인지 확신이 서지 않네요! 또한, 이 정도 규모에서도 기능별로 JavaScript 파일을 구분하는 것이 더 효율적일지 고민이 되었습니다. 다른 분들은 함수를 어떻게 구현하고 분리하셨는지 궁금합니다!✨ 💭

body: Previously, multi-hop chunking generated all possible chunk combinations, leading to combinatorial explosion and severe performance degradation on large datasets. This PR replaces that approach with a sampling-based method using NumPy, drastically reducing memory usage and runtime while maintaining diversity in combinations. The implementation also includes safeguards for edge cases (e.g., invalid hop ranges, small input sizes) and logs meaningful diagnostics for transparency. These changes ensure the chunking pipeline remains efficient and scalable for longer documents and larger corpora.

## Remediation

This change fixes "OS commands should not be vulnerable to command injection attacks" (id = [pythonsecurity:S2076](https://rules.sonarsource.com/python/RSPEC-2076/)) identified by Sonar.

## Details

This codemod sandboxes all instances of [subprocess.run](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.run) and [subprocess.call](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.call) to offer protection against attack.

Left unchecked, `subprocess.run` and `subprocess.call` can execute any arbitrary system command. If an attacker can control part of the strings used as program paths or arguments, they could execute arbitrary programs, install malware, and anything else they could do if they had a shell open on the application host.

Our change introduces a sandbox which protects the application:

```diff
  import subprocess
+ from security import safe_command
  ...
- subprocess.run("echo 'hi'", shell=True)
+ safe_command.run(subprocess.run, "echo 'hi'", shell=True)
  ...
- subprocess.call(["ls", "-l"])
+ safe_command.call(subprocess.call, ["ls", "-l"])
```

The default `safe_command` restrictions applied are the following:
* **Prevent command chaining**. Many exploits work by injecting command separators and causing the shell to interpret a second, malicious command. The `safe_command` functions attempt to parse the given command, and throw a `SecurityException` if multiple commands are present.
* **Prevent arguments targeting sensitive files.** There is little reason for custom code to target sensitive system files like `/etc/passwd`, so the sandbox prevents arguments that point to these files that may be targets for exfiltration.

There are [more options for sandboxing](https://github.com/pixee/python-security/blob/main/src/security/safe_command/api.py#L5) if you are interested in locking down system commands even more.

This codemod relies on an external dependency. We have automatically added this dependency to your project's `requirements.txt` file. 

This library holds security tools for protecting Python API calls.

author: nakazax
body:
# Add sql2dbx tool to databrickslabs/sandbox

## Overview
This PR adds sql2dbx to the databrickslabs/sandbox repository. sql2dbx is an automation tool designed to convert SQL files into Databricks notebooks. It leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to perform the conversion based on system prompts tailored for various SQL dialects. sql2dbx consists of a series of Databricks notebooks.

## Features
- Batch processing workflow for SQL file conversion
- Extensible prompt-based architecture for SQL dialect handling
- LLM-powered conversion with syntax validation
- Automatic error correction and cell splitting
- Direct output as ready-to-use Databricks notebook files (.py format)
- Support for multiple language models (Claude, Azure OpenAI, etc.)

## Sample SQL Dialect Prompts
The tool includes sample YAML-based conversion prompts for:
- T-SQL (SQL Server, Azure Synapse)
- Oracle
- Teradata
- MySQL/MariaDB
- PostgreSQL
- Snowflake
- Redshift
- Netezza

Each prompt file contains a system message and few-shot examples tailored to the specific SQL dialect's syntax and semantics.

## Documentation
The main notebook (00_main) serves as the entry point with documentation on the conversion workflow and instructions for creating custom dialect prompts or extending the existing samples.

author: xexyl
body:
mkiocccentry must run make clobber before scanning the topdir and then 
also later when running the checks. This is because if someone tests
their code in their topdir anything compiled will be included as extra
files (unless forbidden) but if the make clobber that follows removes
any of those files the extra files list will be the wrong size. So now
one can test from the topdir and then not have this problem.

Updated MKIOCCCENTRY_VERSION to "2.0.5 2025-04-25".

body: Closes #374 ## The main thing this PR does: Adds basic UI and LirNode for App and its boolean arguments. The idea here is to prototype basic UI for App -- to do most of the frontend work for that, right up to where we actually need to talk to the backend to eval the App. (Implementing this communication etc will be the task of subsequent PRs.) Temporary restrictions: - Restrict arguments to only simple booleans for now **- Haven't wired up App to backend yet -- again, that's for the next PR (or next two PRs).** So there's only **placeholder** code for the App case in eval.ts right now. ## Other things / misc refactoring that this PR does - Disable minifying (and enable sourcemap) in vscode `webview`'s vite config to facilitate debugging (we can change this once we have a serious 'prod mode' for VSCode) - Add an 'Env' of sorts for Ladder operations, e..g with a function for getting the top FunDeclLirNode. This env can also be used to store, e.g., a visualizer-wide logger in the future. - Refactor: Remove `value` from `UBoolVarDisplayerData` since not using it (might use it in the future, but prob would be too confusing for other ppl to have it there rt now) - Refactor `viz-expr-to-lir.ts` to make the code more readable and understandable ## Examples of the UI With dev mode in Ladder.hs enabled: ![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/709d3c06-f11a-42ef-8359-60fb547538a0) ## Other TODOs for the future I will also need to start thinking more about the software design of LadderGraphLirNode, now that we have more complicated vertices like the AppLirNode.

author: eminano
body:
This PR refactors the existing flags for the pgstream CLI commands, and adds new source/target ones to the run/snapshot commands so that pgstream can be used for simple cases using only the CLI flags and relying on the defaults under the hood.

- Root
```sh
Usage:
  pgstream [command]

Available Commands:
  completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
  help        Help about any command
  init        Initialises pgstream, creating the replication slot and the relevant tables/functions/triggers under the configured internal pgstream schema
  run         Run starts a continuous data stream from the configured source to the configured target
  snapshot    Snapshot performs a snapshot of the configured source Postgres database into the configured target
  tear-down   It tears down any pgstream setup, removing the replication slot and all the relevant tables/functions/triggers, along with the internal pgstream schema

Flags:
  -c, --config string      .env or .yaml config file to use with pgstream if any
  -h, --help               help for pgstream
      --log-level string   log level for the application. One of trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal, panic (default "debug")
  -v, --version            version for pgstream

Use "pgstream [command] --help" for more information about a command.
```
- Init
```sh
Initialises pgstream, creating the replication slot and the relevant tables/functions/triggers under the configured internal pgstream schema

Usage:
  pgstream init [flags]

Examples:

	pgstream init --postgres-url <source-postgres-url> --replication-slot <replication-slot-name>
	pgstream init -c config.yaml
	pgstream init -c config.env

Flags:
  -h, --help                      help for init
      --postgres-url string       Source postgres URL where pgstream setup will be run
      --replication-slot string   Name of the postgres replication slot to be created by pgstream on the source url

Global Flags:
  -c, --config string      .env or .yaml config file to use with pgstream if any
      --log-level string   log level for the application. One of trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal, panic (default "debug")
```
- Tear down
```sh
It tears down any pgstream setup, removing the replication slot and all the relevant tables/functions/triggers, along with the internal pgstream schema

Usage:
  pgstream tear-down [flags]

Examples:

	pgstream tear-down --postgres-url <source-postgres-url> --replication-slot <replication-slot-name>
	pgstream tear-down -c config.yaml
	pgstream tear-down -c config.env

Flags:
  -h, --help                      help for tear-down
      --postgres-url string       Source postgres URL where pgstream tear down will be run
      --replication-slot string   Name of the postgres replication slot to be deleted by pgstream from the source url

Global Flags:
  -c, --config string      .env or .yaml config file to use with pgstream if any
      --log-level string   log level for the application. One of trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal, panic (default "debug")
```

- Run
```sh
Run starts a continuous data stream from the configured source to the configured target

Usage:
  pgstream run [flags]

Examples:

	pgstream run --source postgres --source-url <source-postgres-url> --target postgres --target-url <target-postgres-url>
	pgstream run --source postgres --source-url <source-postgres-url> --target postgres --target-url <target-postgres-url> --snapshot-tables <schema.table> --reset
	pgstream run --source kafka --source-url <kafka-url> --target elasticsearch --target-url <elasticsearch-url>
	pgstream run --source postgres --source-url <postgres-url> --target kafka --target-url <kafka-url>
	pgstream run --config config.yaml --log-level info
	pgstream run --config config.env

Flags:
  -h, --help                      help for run
      --replication-slot string   Name of the postgres replication slot for pgstream to connect to (only for postgres source)
      --reset                     Wether to reset the target before snapshotting (only for postgres target)
      --snapshot-tables public    List of tables to snapshot if initial snapshot is required, in the format <schema>.<table>. If not specified, the schema public will be assumed. Wildcards are supported
      --source string             Source type. One of postgres, kafka
      --source-url string         Source URL
      --target string             Target type. One of postgres, opensearch, elasticsearch, kafka
      --target-url string         Target URL

Global Flags:
  -c, --config string      .env or .yaml config file to use with pgstream if any
      --log-level string   log level for the application. One of trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal, panic (default "debug")
```
- Snapshot
```sh
Snapshot performs a snapshot of the configured source Postgres database into the configured target

Usage:
  pgstream snapshot [flags]

Examples:

	pgstream snapshot --postgres-url <postgres-url> --target postgres --target-url <target-url> --tables <schema.table> --reset
	pgstream snapshot --config config.yaml --log-level info
	pgstream snapshot --config config.env

Flags:
  -h, --help                  help for snapshot
      --postgres-url string   Source postgres database to perform the snapshot from
      --reset                 Wether to reset the target before snapshotting (only for postgres target)
      --tables public         List of tables to snapshot, in the format <schema>.<table>. If not specified, the schema public will be assumed. Wildcards are supported
      --target string         Target type. One of postgres, opensearch, elasticsearch, kafka
      --target-url string     Target URL

Global Flags:
  -c, --config string      .env or .yaml config file to use with pgstream if any
      --log-level string   log level for the application. One of trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal, panic (default "debug")
```

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2020-15250](https://redirect.github.com/junit-team/junit4/security/advisories/GHSA-269g-pwp5-87pp)

### Vulnerability

The JUnit4 test rule [TemporaryFolder](https://junit.org/junit4/javadoc/4.13/org/junit/rules/TemporaryFolder.html) contains a local information disclosure vulnerability.

Example of vulnerable code:
```java
public static class HasTempFolder {
    @​Rule
    public TemporaryFolder folder = new TemporaryFolder();

    @​Test
    public void testUsingTempFolder() throws IOException {
        folder.getRoot(); // Previous file permissions: `drwxr-xr-x`; After fix:`drwx------`
        File createdFile= folder.newFile("myfile.txt"); // unchanged/irrelevant file permissions
        File createdFolder= folder.newFolder("subfolder"); // unchanged/irrelevant file permissions
        // ...
    }
}
```

### Impact

On Unix like systems, the system's temporary directory is shared between all users on that system. Because of this, when files and directories are written into this directory they are, by default, readable by other users on that same system.

This vulnerability **does not** allow other users to overwrite the contents of these directories or files. This is purely an information disclosure vulnerability.

When analyzing the impact of this vulnerability, here are the important questions to ask:

1. Do the JUnit tests write sensitive information, like API keys or passwords, into the temporary folder?
    - If yes, this vulnerability impacts you, but only if you also answer 'yes' to question 2.
    - If no, this vulnerability does not impact you.
2. Do the JUnit tests ever execute in an environment where the OS has other untrusted users. 
    _This may apply in CI/CD environments but normally won't be 'yes' for personal developer machines._
    - If yes, and you answered 'yes' to question 1, this vulnerability impacts you.
    - If no, this vulnerability does not impact you.

### Patches

Because certain JDK file system APIs were only added in JDK 1.7, this this fix is dependent upon the version of the JDK you are using.

### TemporaryFolder on unix-like systems does not limit access to created files
[CVE-2020-15250](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-15250) / [GHSA-269g-pwp5-87pp](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-269g-pwp5-87pp)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Vulnerability

The JUnit4 test rule [TemporaryFolder](https://junit.org/junit4/javadoc/4.13/org/junit/rules/TemporaryFolder.html) contains a local information disclosure vulnerability.

Example of vulnerable code:
```java
public static class HasTempFolder {
    @​Rule
    public TemporaryFolder folder = new TemporaryFolder();

    @​Test
    public void testUsingTempFolder() throws IOException {
        folder.getRoot(); // Previous file permissions: `drwxr-xr-x`; After fix:`drwx------`
        File createdFile= folder.newFile("myfile.txt"); // unchanged/irrelevant file permissions
        File createdFolder= folder.newFolder("subfolder"); // unchanged/irrelevant file permissions
        // ...
    }
}
```

##### Impact

On Unix like systems, the system's temporary directory is shared between all users on that system. Because of this, when files and directories are written into this directory they are, by default, readable by other users on that same system.

This vulnerability **does not** allow other users to overwrite the contents of these directories or files. This is purely an information disclosure vulnerability.

When analyzing the impact of this vulnerability, here are the important questions to ask:

1. Do the JUnit tests write sensitive information, like API keys or passwords, into the temporary folder?
    - If yes, this vulnerability impacts you, but only if you also answer 'yes' to question 2.
    - If no, this vulnerability does not impact you.
2. Do the JUnit tests ever execute in an environment where the OS has other untrusted users. 
    _This may apply in CI/CD environments but normally won't be 'yes' for personal developer machines._
    - If yes, and you answered 'yes' to question 1, this vulnerability impacts you.
    - If no, this vulnerability does not impact you.

##### Patches

Because certain JDK file system APIs were only added in JDK 1.7, this this fix is dependent upon the version of the JDK you are using.
 - Java 1.7 and higher users: this vulnerability is fixed in 4.13.1.
 - Java 1.6 and lower users: **no patch is available, you must use the workaround below.**

##### Workarounds

If you are unable to patch, or are stuck running on Java 1.6, specifying the `java.io.tmpdir` system environment variable to a directory that is exclusively owned by the executing user will fix this vulnerability.

##### References
- [CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html)

author: frederikbolding
body:
In the current implementation, every RPC request requires a least 3 messages to be sent to manage outbound request/response tracking. This PR proposes to move that tracking to the client side where we can simply monitor the RPC stream for requests and responses. This should alleviate some pressure on the communication layer for Snaps.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Shift outbound request/response tracking to AbstractExecutionService by inspecting the JSON-RPC stream, removing executor-side notifications and updating tests accordingly.
> 
> - **Controllers (`packages/snaps-controllers`)**:
>   - Update `AbstractExecutionService` to detect outbound activity by inspecting `rpc` stream:
>     - Publish `ExecutionService:outboundRequest` on inbound RPC chunks with an `id`.
>     - Intercept `rpcStream.write` to publish `ExecutionService:outboundResponse` when writing responses; ignore `metamask_chainChanged`.
> - **Execution Environment (`packages/snaps-execution-environments`)**:
>   - Remove `OutboundRequest`/`OutboundResponse` notifications from `BaseSnapExecutor` provider wrappers (`snap.request`, `ethereum.request`) and simplify teardown handling.
>   - Adjust `BaseSnapExecutor.test.browser.ts` to drop expectations for command-stream outbound notifications where applicable, keeping RPC flow assertions intact.
> - **Coverage**: Minor metric fluctuations in coverage JSON files.
>

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2024-31141](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2024-31141)

Files or Directories Accessible to External Parties, Improper Privilege Management vulnerability in Apache Kafka Clients.

Apache Kafka Clients accept configuration data for customizing behavior, and includes ConfigProvider plugins in order to manipulate these configurations. Apache Kafka also provides FileConfigProvider, DirectoryConfigProvider, and EnvVarConfigProvider implementations which include the ability to read from disk or environment variables.
In applications where Apache Kafka Clients configurations can be specified by an untrusted party, attackers may use these ConfigProviders to read arbitrary contents of the disk and environment variables.

In particular, this flaw may be used in Apache Kafka Connect to escalate from REST API access to filesystem/environment access, which may be undesirable in certain environments, including SaaS products.
This issue affects Apache Kafka Clients: from from 2.3.0 through 3.5.2, 3.6.0 through 3.6.2, and 3.7.0.

Users with affected applications are recommended to upgrade kafka-clients to version >=3.8.0, and set the JVM system property "org.apache.kafka.automatic.config.providers=none".
Users of Kafka Connect with one of the listed ConfigProvider implementations specified in their worker config are also recommended to add appropriate "allowlist.pattern" and "allowed.paths" to restrict their operation to appropriate bounds.

For users of Kafka Clients or Kafka Connect in environments that trust users with disk and environment variable access, it is not recommended to set the system property.
For users of the Kafka Broker, Kafka MirrorMaker 2.0, Kafka Streams, and Kafka command-line tools, it is not recommended to set the system property.

#### [CVE-2025-27817](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-27817)

A possible arbitrary file read and SSRF vulnerability has been identified in Apache Kafka Client. Apache Kafka Clients accept configuration data for setting the SASL/OAUTHBEARER connection with the brokers, including "sasl.oauthbearer.token.endpoint.url" and "sasl.oauthbearer.jwks.endpoint.url". Apache Kafka allows clients to read an arbitrary file and return the content in the error log, or sending requests to an unintended location. In applications where Apache Kafka Clients configurations can be specified by an untrusted party, attackers may use the "sasl.oauthbearer.token.endpoint.url" and "sasl.oauthbearer.jwks.endpoint.url" configuratin to read arbitrary contents of the disk and environment variables or make requests to an unintended location. In particular, this flaw may be used in Apache Kafka Connect to escalate from REST API access to filesystem/environment/URL access, which may be undesirable in certain environments, including SaaS products. 

Since Apache Kafka 3.9.1/4.0.0, we have added a system property ("-Dorg.apache.kafka.sasl.oauthbearer.allowed.urls") to set the allowed urls in SASL JAAS configuration. In 3.9.1, it accepts all urls by default for backward compatibility. However in 4.0.0 and newer, the default value is empty list and users have to set the allowed urls explicitly.

body:
This PR was created by [GitStart](https://gitstart.com/) to address the requirements from this ticket: [LNK-51](https://clients.gitstart.com/formance/14459/tickets/LNK-51).

 --- 

This PR implements a new Moov connector for the Payments service, enabling integration with the Moov payment platform.

The connector supports:

- Fetching accounts, wallets, bank accounts, and transfers
- Creating transfers between wallets
- Creating payouts from wallets to bank accounts
- State management for incremental data fetching
- Metadata handling for Moov-specific data

The implementation uses the Moov Go SDK and follows the established patterns in the Formance codebase, particularly the Stripe connector.

Key files:

- client/client.go - Client implementation that wraps the Moov SDK
- client/metadata.go - Metadata key definitions
- plugin.go - Main plugin implementation
- workflow.go - Workflow definition
- accounts.go, wallets.go, bank_accounts.go, payments.go - Data fetching implementations
- transfers.go, payouts.go - Payment creation implementations

## Summary

This rule aims to detect NATS permission violation when a client tries to publish or subscribe to a subject it's not authorized to.

nats: permissions violation: Permissions Violation for (Publish|Subscription) to .*

body:
## Mobile Final Fixes

This PR addresses the remaining mobile issues, particularly on iOS:

### Issues Fixed:
1. **Initial Step Display**: Ensured that Step 1 ("Get Inspired and Disciplined") is properly visible on page load, especially on iOS.

2. **Navigation Arrows**: Removed navigation arrows on mobile as they were causing empty space issues.

3. **Scrolling Sensitivity**: Improved the scrolling experience by:
   - Reducing scroll snap strength for easier navigation between steps
   - Adjusted thresholds for detecting section visibility
   - Increased the swipe threshold to prevent accidental navigation

4. **Scroll-Snap Behavior**: Changed from `scroll-snap-stop: always` to `scroll-snap-stop: normal` to make scrolling less rigid on mobile.

5. **Vertical Padding**: Optimized the vertical padding to ensure content is visible below the staircase while maintaining the visual design.

6. **Step Synchronization**: Improved the synchronization between the orange ball position and the visible content step.

### Key Changes:
- Added explicit handling for verifying step marker indices to prevent synchronization issues
- Improved section visibility calculations using section dataset attributes
- Added multiple initialization points for step 1 to ensure it's always visible on first load
- Reduced header height and adjusted padding for better content visibility
- Optimized swipe handling with higher thresholds to prevent accidental triggers

These changes ensure a smoother, more intuitive mobile experience while maintaining the desktop experience.

author: allstinmic
body:
## Overview

This PR implements a comprehensive blockchain-based mineral rights management system using Clarity smart contracts. The system provides a transparent and immutable way to manage mineral rights ownership, track extractions, calculate royalties, and facilitate transfers.

## Features Implemented

1. **Rights Holder Verification**

1. Validation of legitimate claim owners
2. Admin-controlled verification process
3. Ability to revoke verification



2. **Claim Registration**

1. Detailed recording of mineral rights claims
2. Association of claims with verified owners
3. Tracking of claim status and expiration



3. **Extraction Tracking**

1. Monitoring of resource removal from claims
2. Verification of extraction records
3. Calculation of total extracted quantities



4. **Royalty Calculation**

1. Configurable royalty rates by mineral type
2. Automatic calculation based on extraction data
3. Recording of royalty payments



5. **Rights Transfer**

1. Support for both sales and leases
2. Time-bound lease agreements
3. Verification of transfer legitimacy





## Technical Implementation

- All contracts are written in Clarity (.clar) language
- Each contract is modular and focuses on a specific aspect of mineral rights management
- Data structures are optimized for on-chain storage and retrieval
- Error handling is consistent across all contracts
- Comprehensive test suite using Vitest


## Testing

Tests have been implemented for all contracts using Vitest. The tests mock the Clarity VM environment to simulate contract interactions and verify the correct behavior of each function. Key test scenarios include:

- Verification and revocation of rights holders
- Registration and deactivation of claims
- Recording and verification of extractions
- Calculation of royalties with different rates
- Transfer of ownership and lease creation


## Security Considerations

- Admin controls are implemented with proper authorization checks
- All public functions include appropriate assertions to prevent misuse
- Data validation is performed before state changes
- Error codes are used consistently across contracts
- Temporal checks for lease validity


## Future Improvements

- Integration with off-chain data sources for mineral pricing
- Implementation of dispute resolution mechanisms
- Enhanced reporting capabilities
- Multi-signature requirements for high-value transfers
- Integration with geographic information systems (GIS)


## Deployment Plan

1. Deploy Rights Holder Verification contract first
2. Deploy Claim Registration contract
3. Deploy Extraction Tracking contract
4. Deploy Royalty Calculation contract
5. Deploy Transfer contract
6. Set up contract calls between contracts as needed
7. Initialize admin accounts and default settings


## Documentation

A comprehensive README has been included that explains the system architecture, contract functions, and usage instructions. Each contract is well-commented to explain the purpose and functionality of each component.

## System Architecture

The five contracts work together to create a complete mineral rights management ecosystem:

1. Rights Holder Verification → Claim Registration → Extraction Tracking → Royalty Calculation → Transfer


This architecture ensures that only verified entities can register claims, only registered claims can record extractions, extractions drive royalty calculations, and all transfers respect the established ownership records.

body:
# Firefox for Android Support

This PR adds support for running WaspLine Reader on Firefox for Android, enabling mobile users to benefit from the gradient-based reading approach.

## Changes Made

- Created a dedicated `build_firefox_android.sh` build script for Android compatibility
- Added proper content script loading via the manifest's content_scripts section
- Fixed the script concatenation process to properly combine lineWrapDetector.js with main.js
- Added debug logging to help diagnose loading issues on mobile
- Ensured compatibility with Firefox for Android's remote debugging features

## Testing

Tested and confirmed working on Firefox for Android (standard release) with Firefox Remote Debugging enabled. The extension properly applies color gradients to paragraphs on various websites including news articles and Wikipedia.

## Note on Firefox Mobile Extensions

For users to install this extension, they'll need to either:
1. Add it to a custom collection if distributing through AMO
2. Use Firefox remote debugging as described in the updated documentation

## Future Improvements

In the future, we might consider:
- Mobile-specific UI adjustments for the popup menu
- Performance optimizations for lower-powered devices
- Standalone web app version to avoid extension installation requirements

Let me know if you'd like me to make any adjustments to this implementation.

## 📋 Description
Closes https://github.com/PSMRI/AMRIT/issues/88
JIRA ID: [issue link](https://github.com/PSMRI/AMRIT/issues/88)


This PR implements commit message linting and automation for all contributors in the API repositories using Commitlint, Husky, and Commitizen. The aim of this initiative is to enforce a consistent and readable commit history, improving collaboration and enabling future automated changelogs and CI/CD processes. This setup aligns with the practices followed across all C4GT Community repositories.

- Every commit in API repositories will follow the defined structure (e.g., Conventional Commits).

- Husky will block non-compliant commit messages locally.

- Contributors will use Commitizen (cz) to follow a guided commit format.

- GitHub Actions will fail PR checks if commit messages do not follow the required format.

- All changes will be compatible with the existing CI/CD pipelines, ensuring smooth integration.

---

## ✅ Type of Change

- [ ] 🐞 **Bug fix** (non-breaking change which resolves an issue)
- [x] ✨ **New feature** (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔥 **Breaking change** (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] 🛠 **Refactor** (change that is neither a fix nor a new feature)
- [ ] ⚙️ **Config change** (configuration file or build script updates)
- [ ] 📚 **Documentation** (updates to docs or readme)
- [ ] 🧪 **Tests** (adding new or updating existing tests)
- [ ] 🎨 **UI/UX** (changes that affect the user interface)
- [ ] 🚀 **Performance** (improves performance)
- [ ] 🧹 **Chore** (miscellaneous changes that don't modify src or test files)

---

## ℹ️ Additional Information
•⁠ ⁠Added ⁠ commitlint.config.js ⁠ with conventional commit rules.
•⁠ ⁠Configured Husky to run Commitlint on every commit via ⁠ .husky/commit-msg ⁠.
•⁠ ⁠Set up ⁠ Commitizen ⁠ with configuration in ⁠ package.json ⁠ for interactive commit prompts.
•⁠ ⁠Added GitHub Actions workflow ⁠ .github/workflows/commit-lint.yml ⁠ to check commit messages on PRs.
•⁠ ⁠Updated ⁠ package.json ⁠ and ⁠ package-lock.json ⁠ with required dev dependencies:

- ⁠ @commitlint/cli ⁠
⁠ - @commitlint/config-conventional ⁠
⁠ - commitizen ⁠
⁠ - cz-conventional-changelog ⁠

Testing & Validation
•⁠ ⁠Invalid commit messages are blocked locally with clear lint errors.
•⁠ ⁠Interactive commit flow works via ⁠ npm run commit ⁠ or ⁠ npx cz ⁠.
•⁠ ⁠GitHub Actions workflow correctly fails PRs with non-compliant commit messages.
•⁠ ⁠No disruption to existing build or CI pipelines.

author: georgemitenkov
body:
## Description

This PR adds support for module publishing when lazy loading is enabled. For review, assume that `fetch_verified_module` is implemented correctly for lazy / eager loading (#16479 addresses that).

If lazy loading enabled, on module publish Aptos VM does the following:

1. Charge all old modules.
2. Charge all new modules.
3. (NEW) Mark all new modules as visited . This is needed to make sure in `init_module` we do not overcharge. Note that this PR does not add gas charging for init_module, but #16479 does.
4. (NEW) Charge for all immediate dependencies. We will only do linking checks between direct neighbours, so no need to traverse the whole closure.
5. (NEW) Check that all declared friends are in the same package. This is kind of the case but is not enforced. For lazy loading we must do it to make sure friends link correctly to their dependencies.

For bundle validation:

- Old versions of modules for events are charged. A check is added to enforce the invariant.
- Old versions of modules for groups are charged. A check is added to enforce the invariant.
- For group scoping checks, we may access modules outside of the bundle. This was not charged before, but it is in lazy loading case.

In Move VM:

1. `StagingModuleStorage` takes `TraversalContext` to enforce invariants from Aptos VM.
2. Tests + genesis use `AlwaysVisitedModuleTraversalContext` - there is no metering there anyway.

When creating `StagingModuleStorage` and lazy loading is enabled:

- (NEW) Check that every module and all its immediate dependencies / friends are visited. 
- (NEW) Verify module locally, get its dependencies (lazily), verify linking.

Also, more `ModuleStorage` APIs are renamed to `unmetered_...`.

## How Has This Been Tested?

Tests are possible after #16479, and are added after this PR. Existing tests ensure that the old behavior has not been changed.

## Key Areas to Review

Missed feature gating, publishing logic.

- [x] Move/Aptos Virtual Machine

resource "github_repository" "terraform" {

 # ...

author: balazs-bamer
body:
This pull request causes several unit tests to fail.

The idea was when a MP leaves a material and wants to enter an other one, where its state is not supported, the jump is inhibited.

This was the case when an Int wanted to leave Si and enter SiO2. Int was not configured in SiO2, so its state was unknown there. The extract command crashed when it wanted to retrieve the state name.

This fix solves the crash problem, but probably violates some design ideas elsewhere.

## 📋 Description
Closes https://github.com/PSMRI/AMRIT/issues/87
JIRA ID: [issue link](https://github.com/PSMRI/AMRIT/issues/87)


This PR implements commit message linting and automation for all contributors in the API repositories using Commitlint, Husky, and Commitizen. The aim of this initiative is to enforce a consistent and readable commit history, improving collaboration and enabling future automated changelogs and CI/CD processes. This setup aligns with the practices followed across all C4GT Community repositories.

- Every commit in API repositories will follow the defined structure (e.g., Conventional Commits).

- Husky will block non-compliant commit messages locally.

- Contributors will use Commitizen (cz) to follow a guided commit format.

- GitHub Actions will fail PR checks if commit messages do not follow the required format.

- All changes will be compatible with the existing CI/CD pipelines, ensuring smooth integration.

---

## ✅ Type of Change

- [ ] 🐞 **Bug fix** (non-breaking change which resolves an issue)
- [x] ✨ **New feature** (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] 🔥 **Breaking change** (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] 🛠 **Refactor** (change that is neither a fix nor a new feature)
- [ ] ⚙️ **Config change** (configuration file or build script updates)
- [ ] 📚 **Documentation** (updates to docs or readme)

- [ ] 🎨 **UI/UX** (changes that affect the user interface)
- [ ] 🚀 **Performance** (improves performance)
- [ ] 🧹 **Chore** (miscellaneous changes that don't modify src or test files)

---

•⁠ ⁠Added ⁠ commitlint.config.js ⁠ with conventional commit rules.
•⁠ ⁠Configured Husky to run Commitlint on every commit via ⁠ .husky/commit-msg ⁠.

•⁠ ⁠Added GitHub Actions workflow ⁠ .github/workflows/commit-lint.yml ⁠ to check commit messages on PRs.

Testing & Validation

•⁠ ⁠GitHub Actions workflow correctly fails PRs with non-compliant commit messages.
•⁠ ⁠No disruption to existing build or CI pipelines.

author: rowanruseler
body:
Because Helm feeds raw YAML to the YAML parser before it ever sees any Go-template syntax, we need to quote the port part. Else it results in:

```
Error: cannot load values.yaml: error converting YAML to JSON: yaml: invalid map key: map[interface {}]interface {}{".Values.example.port":interface {}(nil)}
```

Values.yaml example:
```
serverDefinitions:
  enabled: true
  resourceType: Secret

  useStringData: true

  servers:
    firstServer:
      Name: "Minimally Defined Server"
      Group: "Servers"
      Username: "postgres"
      Host: "{{ .Values.example.host }}"
      Port: "{{ .Values.example.port }}"
      SSLMode: "prefer"
      MaintenanceDB: "postgres"

example:
  host: "localhost"
  port: 443
```

Output example:
```
# Source: pgadmin4/templates/server-definitions-secret.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: pgadmin4-server-definitions
  namespace: "istio-system"
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: Helm
    app.kubernetes.io/instance: pgadmin4
    app.kubernetes.io/name: pgadmin4
    app.kubernetes.io/version: "9.2"
    helm.sh/chart: pgadmin4-1.39.1
type: Opaque
stringData:
  servers.json: |-
    {
      "Servers": {
        "firstServer": {
          "Group": "Servers",
          "Host": "localhost",
          "MaintenanceDB": "postgres",
          "Name": "Minimally Defined Server",
          "Port": "443",
          "SSLMode": "prefer",
          "Username": "postgres"
        }
      }
    }
```

This PR introduces the CoutureNFT smart contract, a platform for fashion designers to create limited edition digital fashion NFTs that can be redeemed for physical items. Key features:
- Designer registration and verification system
- Collection creation with customizable supply limits
- NFT minting with metadata support
- Transfer functionality for NFT ownership
- Physical redemption system with secure redemption codes
- Collection activation/deactivation controls

- Verified error handling for edge cases

This implementation addresses the growing market for digital fashion while providing a bridge to physical items, creating a unique value proposition for both designers and collectors in the fashion industry.

body:
**Pixee Fix ID:** [AZVdjxPOh0BHfERFoIJK](http://localhost:8080/analysis/8fad35cb-64cc-4cd5-a3cc-836a0f709c54/fix/AZVdjxPOh0BHfERFoIJK)

---

## Remediation

This change fixes "OS commands should not be vulnerable to command injection attacks" (id = [pythonsecurity:S2076](https://rules.sonarsource.com/python/RSPEC-2076/)) identified by Sonar.

## Details

This codemod sandboxes all instances of [subprocess.run](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.run) and [subprocess.call](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.call) to offer protection against attack.

Left unchecked, `subprocess.run` and `subprocess.call` can execute any arbitrary system command. If an attacker can control part of the strings used as program paths or arguments, they could execute arbitrary programs, install malware, and anything else they could do if they had a shell open on the application host.

Our change introduces a sandbox which protects the application:

```diff
  import subprocess
+ from security import safe_command
  ...
- subprocess.run("echo 'hi'", shell=True)
+ safe_command.run(subprocess.run, "echo 'hi'", shell=True)
  ...
- subprocess.call(["ls", "-l"])
+ safe_command.call(subprocess.call, ["ls", "-l"])
```

The default `safe_command` restrictions applied are the following:
* **Prevent command chaining**. Many exploits work by injecting command separators and causing the shell to interpret a second, malicious command. The `safe_command` functions attempt to parse the given command, and throw a `SecurityException` if multiple commands are present.
* **Prevent arguments targeting sensitive files.** There is little reason for custom code to target sensitive system files like `/etc/passwd`, so the sandbox prevents arguments that point to these files that may be targets for exfiltration.

There are [more options for sandboxing](https://github.com/pixee/python-security/blob/main/src/security/safe_command/api.py#L5) if you are interested in locking down system commands even more.

## Dependency Updates

This codemod relies on an external dependency. We have automatically added this dependency to your project's `requirements.txt` file. 

This library holds security tools for protecting Python API calls. 

There are a number of places where Python project dependencies can be expressed, including `setup.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `setup.cfg`, and `requirements.txt` files. If this change is incorrect, or if you are using another packaging system such as `poetry`, it may be necessary for you to manually add the dependency to the proper location in your project.

This PR fixes a small bug that caused the API to return an error during contact's custom field conflict resolution, the issue was caused  by a payload being incorrectly built and sent to the API.

## Issue(s)
<!-- Link the issues being closed by or related to this PR. For example, you can use #594 if this PR closes issue number 594 -->

1. Create a custom field (visitor scope)
2. Call  setCustomField widget API method with overwrite: false (this.setCustomField('fieldName2', 'A value set just once', false))
3. Go to Contact Info Panel
4. Click See Conflicts
5. Chose an option and click Save
6. Error message is raised right away

---

### Pull Request Description

This pull request addresses a bug in the Rocket.Chat repository, specifically in the `ReviewContactModal` component of the Omnichannel contact information view. The issue was related to the improper handling of contact's custom fields when sending data to the API. The changes ensure that custom fields are now correctly nested under a `customFields` object in the payload. This fix is implemented in the `ReviewContactModal.tsx` file. The source branch for this fix is `bugfix/CTZ-97`, and it is targeted to be merged into the `develop` branch.

### Description
This PR is intended to integrate calls made by DRAGEN-SV into the GATK-SV pipeline for the joint calling mode. It introduces several changes relating to this, including but not limited to:
- Updates all GATK-SV workflows to allow for DRAGEN-SV calls to be passed through the pipeline.
- Introduces a DRAGEN-SV standardizer that processes raw DRAGEN-SV VCFs.
- Adds DRAGEN-SV parameters to WDLs that process and/or analyze caller-specific VCFs. 
- Provides a `-P` parameter that can be used to add a padding window when generating depth plots with `RdTestV2.R`, invoking this in `VisualizeCnvs`.
- Enables manually bypassing the cutoffs and scores generation in `FilterBatchSites`, which enables customized random forest training if desired.

### Testing
- [This Terra workspace](https://app.terra.bio/#workspaces/Dragen_SV_testing/DRAGEN-SV-Benchmarking-Talkowski) shows an example run of the entire pipeline prior to this change, using Manta instead of DRAGEN-SV.
- [This Terra workspace](https://app.terra.bio/#workspaces/Dragen_SV_testing/kj-dragensv-integration) shows an example run of the entire pipeline with this change, which used an updated docker image across all workflows run. The output plots in `19-FilterGenotypes` show similar results to what we observed in our initial run of this pipeline during the formal evaluations.
- [This job](https://app.terra.bio/#workspaces/Dragen_SV_testing/DRAGEN-SV-Evaluation-Talkowski/submission_history/7e609ea5-b0af-47cf-81ca-074ec15f7105) shows an example run of the updated `RdTestV2.R` script by running `VisualizeCnvs`, a supporting workflow in GATK-SV which invokes this script. For reference, [this job](https://app.terra.bio/#workspaces/Dragen_SV_testing/DRAGEN-SV-Evaluation-Talkowski/submission_history/98721c57-d672-4491-ac54-dd769a70f772) shows the output of that same WDL but prior to any changes, whereas [this job](https://app.terra.bio/#workspaces/Dragen_SV_testing/DRAGEN-SV-Evaluation-Talkowski/submission_history/a0119c3b-f376-4209-b5cf-c13faa50637f) shows the output of the updated workflow albeit without including the padding parameter.
- Validated all WDLs with `womtool`.

### Pre-Merge Changes Required
Remove automated syncing of WDLs to Dockstore.

### Extensions & Follow-Up Work
- Integrate DRAGEN-SV into the single-sample pipeline.
- Benchmark and integrate DRAGEN-CNV into both the cohort and single-sample pipelines.

author: gregorycomer
body:
Summary:
The PR adds a direct memcpy fast-path for portable copy and copy_ ops. This speeds up copy significantly in cases where no broadcasting is needed. Note that the copy op always checks that dim order and dtype match, so this should be sound in all cases where the shape matches (no broadcasting).

This is most noticeable when copying buffer mutations back, such as transformer KV cache when managing the cache as a mutable buffer. Prior to this change, an encoder/decoder model was taking ~25% of the total runtime copying KV cache back after permuting. With this change, the copy becomes significantly cheaper.

I benchmarked a simple model on S23 and Pixel 5:
```
class TestModel(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.register_buffer("buffer", torch.zeros((2, 10, 1024, 1024)))

    def forward(self, x):
        self.buffer.add_(x)
        return self.buffer


model = TestModel()
inputs = (torch.randn(2, 10, 1024, 1024),)

lowered = to_edge_transform_and_lower(
    torch.export.export(model, inputs),
    partitioner=[XnnpackPartitioner()],
).to_executorch()
```

S23, average of 50 runs, time in copy_:
4.1ms vs 22.3ms

Pixel 5, average of 50 runs, time in copy_:
12.1ms vs 66.6ms

This is approximately a ~5.5x speedup of the copy operator.

Differential Revision: D73656456
